Poetic form: Rhymed couplet
Two successive verse lines share an end rhyme. A closed couplet also completes a grammatical unit.
Pattern: AA.

Poetic form: Tercet
A three-line stanza. Its lines may rhyme or remain unrhymed; the line count alone does not specify a complete rhyme scheme.

Poetic form: Quatrain
A stanza of four lines. Common arrangements include alternating rhymes and paired rhymes.
Possible patterns: ABAB or AABB.

Poetic form: Ballad stanza
A common English narrative stanza alternates four-beat and three-beat lines, with the second and fourth lines rhyming.
Typical rhyme arrangement: ABCB.
